pretreatments.description: Milling: The macralgal biomass (Laminaria sp.) was subjected to mechanical degradation using a Hollander beater machine to reduce particle size and increase specific surface area before anaerobic digestion.

Thermal treatment: The sludge was subjected to a thermal treatment process to improve its dewaterability and destroy pathogens, involving heating the material to high temperatures (specifically 175°C is mentioned as the ideal target).
Chemical treatment: Hydrogen peroxide was applied to sludge to reduce its volume by 30% and improve its dewaterability.
Physical treatment (Mechanical): Ultrasound was used on sludge particles at 37°C to disintegrate sludge particles and produce extra biogas.

Pre-treatment: Mechanical pretreatment (using a Hollander beater) was applied to the macroalgae biomass (Pelvetia Caniculata, Fucus Serratus, Gracilaria Gracilis, Fucus Vesiculosus, and Laminaria Digitata) prior to anaerobic digestion.
Chemical treatment: Drying was performed at 105°C to obtain constant weight and calculate moisture content of both untreated and treated material samples.
Hydrogen peroxide treatment: Applied to sludge to reduce volume by 30%.
Appels treatment: 40% extra biogas was obtained for low frequency ultrasound treatment at 37°C.
Milling: Applied to maize silage (not algae, but mentioned as a reference for the Hollander beater's effectiveness). Not applied to algae in this study.
